title: Shadow IT Report (also SaaS Security Report, ZINS): shadow IT discovery, risk index and API surface

prose.text: IoT device visibility is in the IoT Report, not this one: {{ssr-iot-report}} {{gap:ssr-iot}}. Whether it is powered by ZIA traffic is open {{gap:ssr-zia}}. Whether it is observability only, with no enforcement, is open {{gap:ssr-enforcement}}.
{{ssr-endpoint}} {{ssr-sdk}} The GraphQL API itself, its auth and its scope are in [[shared.analytics.graphql]].

The legacy statement that neither SDK has a zins namespace is contradicted for Python {{gap:ssr-no-sdk}}. {{divergence:report-name}} The rename history is not captured {{gap:ssr-rename}}. The 8,500-app figure in older marketing is in no capture {{gap:ssr-8500}}. {{ssr-scale|ref}}

checks.do: Before comparing shadow IT counts, confirm the time period and filters; the default period is the last 7 days.
For an API question, check the zins package and the GraphQL endpoint before saying there is no SDK; the Python SDK has one.

quotes: The Shadow IT gives a breakdown of applications by their status — sanctioned, unsanctioned, unclassified, or under review and their number of users.

ssr-scale.statement: Zscaler says the report supports up to 50K cloud applications.

quotes: Zscaler supports up to 50K cloud applications.

quotes: (1–5, 1 being the lowest risk and 5 being the highest)

ssr-rename.title: Whether the product was renamed from the Shadow IT Report
ssr-rename.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Renamed. Originally "Shadow IT Report" (ZINS naming), now marketed as "SaaS Security Report" in current help docs.' The report's own page now names it the Shadow IT Report, so the legacy direction (Shadow IT first, SaaS Security later) is not supported by page text; the old URL survives only as an alias in capture metadata. The Python SDK calls the domain Z-Insights SHADOW_IT, which supports the ZINS alias but not the rename history.

ssr-iot.title: Whether the SaaS Security Report gives IoT device visibility
ssr-iot.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Reporting product covering Shadow IT discovery (unsanctioned cloud apps users access), IoT device visibility, and SaaS-app risk reporting.' The SaaS Security Report capture does not mention IoT devices; IoT device visibility is described by a separate capture (about-iot-report.json).
ssr-iot.resolution: Resolved: IoT device inventory is in the IoT Report (claim ssr-iot-report), not the SaaS Security Report.

ssr-zia.title: Whether the SaaS Security Report is powered by ZIA traffic
ssr-zia.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Powered by traffic flowing through ZIA; extracts visibility signals from existing ZIA telemetry.' The capture places the report under Data Security > Inline CASB > Shadow IT and mentions allowed and blocked transactions, but does not state its data source.

ssr-enforcement.title: Whether the SaaS Security Report enforces policy
ssr-enforcement.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Not a policy-enforcement product; pure observability.' The capture describes discovery, risk review and reporting, and says nothing about enforcement either way.

ssr-8500.title: Older catalogue size in marketing material
ssr-8500.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Some marketing material still cites the older 8,500+ figure — outdated.' No captured page gives an 8,500-application figure.
ssr-8500.resolution: Resolved: no captured page gives an 8,500 figure; the current help states up to 50K cloud applications (claim ssr-scale).

ssr-no-sdk.title: Whether the Go SDK has a Z-Insights module
ssr-no-sdk.detail: The vendored Go SDK tree has no zins package, so Go callers would use direct GraphQL with OneAPI auth; upstream Go releases newer than the vendored tree are unchecked. The Python SDK does have one (ssr-sdk).

report-name.summary: The report's own page and the audit-log page call it the Shadow IT Report, while the NSS page still says SaaS Security Report; whether they mean the same report is not stated.
